replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body:
software engineer here.  hard disagree.  subs have purposes; that's why nobody's in here asking for resume advice or help with their soup recipe.  categorization is critical to a healthy and functioning sub, and doing it wrong can r/opensource you.

categorization is not a dichotomy in any sense (yes, i know you're going to say "in" and "out", and no, that doesn't fit this usage if you think about it.)  as a result it cannot be a false dichotomy.

it is useful to know what is appropriate in here.

is this a place to discuss development technique?  a place to show off your work?  both?

OP is correct to ask.  And for my part, I hope the answer is "both."

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body:
Software engineer here. Sorry to disagree : if Claude is coding, you're reviewing. And if you're not reviewing, then you're just an art director with a yolo coder.

The same for AI art, if Midjourney is drawing, you're just curating.

And if, in 10 years, an android is cooking, you're not cooking. You're just the owner of an android cooker.

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body:
If you use a linter, you are coding. If you use tab-autocomplete, you are coding. If you use Copilot to generate a function, you are coding. If Claude writes an entire implementation and you review, debug, test, and integrate it, you are coding. You never stop being a software engineer at any of those milestones in automation.

Programming isn't simply the physical act of typing code any more than photography is the physical act of exposing film or cooking is the physical act of chopping vegetables. Treating these as binaries makes no sense, and most what you did before was vibed anyways — just like cooking.

TLDR: Stop gatekeeping, it's cringe as fuck.

replies.author: fisj
replies.body:
There's not a lot of good options mods have here. Making a rule to not discuss the use of AI is obviously stupid. It's a large and important part of our community figuring out what AI works for and doesn't. We could add flair, but flair is pretty ineffective (imho).

When people bring up "there's too many discussions of X", its usually part of the ebb and flow of what things get talked about a lot, then die back down. I'm not convinced this is an issue, but help us mods understand if you all feel strongly about it.

In an ideal universe, every redditor would have an AI filter the things they dislike perfectly.

comments.author: CandidateDue2480
comments.body:
It's a majority people sharing their prototypes, or getting into the AI culture war.

It's sparse finding developer-oriented content. 

I work in a known studio so I can't really share certain practices yet, I know others in the same boat. More importantly there's a lot of apprehension around knowledge share due to the stigma; even an invite only, private dev server I'm on has very few developers openly sharing knowledge due to the stigma.

Hoping for the Gold Rush to fade out a bit and those still tooling on their projects in six months will get more technical oriented as they hit the problems past prototype.
